verdict.rationale: Calendly documents ways to issue API credentials: personal access tokens for internal apps and OAuth 2.1 for public apps. Its MCP server uses OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration, so an agent can get its own delegated credential without pre-registering an app. However, nothing in the evidence shows these credentials can be scoped or restricted to least privilege. Missing for 10: documented OAuth scopes or PAT permission scoping, read-only or resource-limited tokens, agent-specific credential restriction or revocation controls, independent corroboration.
